issues.description: Story loading requires data/stories/manifest.json and per-story files, but the repo does not ship them or provide a fallback generation path.
The primary tiny end-to-end integration test fails on a clean checkout because the required story corpus is missing.
The advertised demo script calls the broken tiny extraction path, so make demo is not reproducible from the repository.
Checked-in generated outputs reference a source story manifest that is not present, masking stale and unreproducible artifacts.
Validation recreates the backend from CLI flags instead of enforcing compatibility with the vector manifest backend, layer count, and model dimension.
Preference steering loads vector artifacts without checking that the selected backend matches the manifest, risking crashes or invalid results.
Vector artifacts are loaded without shape, dtype, emotion-count, or layer-count validation before downstream indexing.
A manifest with emotions not present in SCENARIOS causes an empty np.stack crash instead of a clear validation error.
Tiny backend emotion matching uses substring counts, causing false emotion signals from unrelated words that merely contain lexicon terms.
HF steering falls back to all prompt tokens when token offsets are unavailable, violating the intended activity-token-only intervention.
HF activation extraction has no truncation, batching, or max-token guard, so long inputs can cause avoidable memory failures.
Preference scoring assumes the first token of ' good' and ' bad' is a valid comparable scalar across tokenizers and models.
pca_components_for_variance(threshold=0) still returns one component, contradicting the stated threshold semantics.
steering.min_reported_emotions from config.yaml is ignored and the implementation hardcodes four steered emotions.
Dependencies are only lower-bounded and there is no lockfile, reducing reproducibility for a numerical pipeline.
CLI commands allow raw tracebacks for expected setup and data errors instead of returning actionable user-facing messages.
